---
title: "Plot Type Stability"
description: "Which py-maidr plot types are settled and which are experimental prototypes that may change without a deprecation period."
html-table-processing: none
---

## Two sets, two different promises

`PlotType` in `maidr/core/enum/plot_type.py` names **44** plot types. They do
not all carry the same promise, and nothing in the enum says so — which is what
this page is for.

Fifteen of them predate the plot coverage roadmap
([#345](https://github.com/xability/py-maidr/issues/345)). Twenty-three were
added by it, most inside about two weeks, and `ROC`, `RUG`, `RIDGELINE`,
`DIRECTED_GRAPH`, `PERCENTILE_BAND` and `PR_CURVE` after it. **None of the
twenty-nine has been through a user study**.

Elsewhere in these docs — the example gallery, the navigation and the
supported-plots lists on the home page — an experimental type is marked
**[experimental]** after its name; a type with no mark is stable. A list of
plot types is also split in two, a Stable part followed by an Experimental
part; the navigation puts the example pages about experimental types only in
a group of their own after the stable ones; and a gallery page shows its
stable charts before its experimental ones. The JavaScript core ([Trace type stability](https://maidr.ai/docs/SCHEMA.html#trace-type-stability))
and maidr for R ([Supported plot types](https://r.maidr.ai/#supported-plot-types))
mark their own docs the same way.

## Stable

| `PlotType` | emitted as | drawn by |
|---|---|---|
| `BAR` | `bar` | `ax.bar`, `sns.barplot` |
| `BOX` | `box` | `ax.boxplot`, `sns.boxplot` |
| `CANDLESTICK` | `candlestick` | `mplfinance` |
| `COUNT` | `count` | `sns.countplot` |
| `DODGED` | `dodged_bar` | grouped bars |
| `HEAT` | `heat` | `ax.imshow`, `sns.heatmap` |
| `HIST` | `hist` | `ax.hist`, `sns.histplot` |
| `LINE` | `line` | `ax.plot`, `sns.lineplot` |
| `PIE` | `pie` | `ax.pie` |
| `SCATTER` | `point` | `ax.scatter`, `sns.scatterplot` |
| `SMOOTH` | `smooth` | `sns.regplot`, `sns.lmplot` |
| `STACKED` | `stacked_bar` | stacked bars |
| `STEP` | `step` | `ax.step` |
| `VIOLIN_BOX` | `violin_box` | `sns.violinplot` |
| `VIOLIN_KDE` | `violin_kde` | `sns.violinplot` |

These are what py-maidr was built around. Their extraction, their announcements
and their keyboard model have been exercised by real users over real charts, and
changing any of them changes behavior people already depend on.

## Experimental

::: {.callout-warning title="Prototypes"}
**These are prototypes. Treat them as prototypes.** They are under active
development, they are unstable, and they have not been validated with the
readers they are for.
:::

| `PlotType` | emitted as |
|---|---|
| `ALLUVIAL` | `alluvial` |
| `AREA` | `area` |
| `BOXEN` | `boxen` |
| `CHOROPLETH` | `choropleth` |
| `CONTOUR` | `contour` |
| `DIRECTED_GRAPH` | `directed_graph` |
| `ERRORBAR` | `error_bar` |
| `FUNNEL` | `funnel` |
| `GANTT` | `gantt` |
| `GAUGE` | `gauge` |
| `HEXBIN` | `hexbin` |
| `ICICLE` | `icicle` |
| `LOLLIPOP` | `lollipop` |
| `NORMALIZED` | `stacked_normalized_bar` |
| `NORMALIZED_AREA` | `stacked_normalized_area` |
| `PARALLEL` | `parallel_coordinates` |
| `PERCENTILE_BAND` | `percentile_band` |
| `POLAR_AREA` | `polar_area` |
| `PR_CURVE` | `pr_curve` |
| `RADAR` | `radar` |
| `RIDGELINE` | `ridgeline` |
| `ROC` | `roc` |
| `RUG` | `rug` |
| `SANKEY` | `sankey` |
| `STACKED_AREA` | `stacked_area` |
| `SUNBURST` | `sunburst` |
| `TREEMAP` | `treemap` |
| `WATERFALL` | `waterfall` |
| `WORD_CLOUD` | `word_cloud` |

What that means, concretely:

- **Under active development.** These are being changed as they are used, not
  maintained against a settled specification.
- **Unstable.** Field names, announcement wording and navigation semantics may
  change without a deprecation period, including in a patch release. Code that
  depends on the exact shape one of these emits is pinned to the py-maidr
  version it was written against.
- **Not validated.** Each was measured against the chart it reads — that is what
  the issues and the tests record. But measuring that a reading is *faithful to
  the drawing* is a different claim from establishing that it is *useful to a
  reader*. Nobody has asked a blind or low-vision reader whether navigating a
  sunburst by depth, or hearing each parallel-coordinates axis on its own scale,
  is the right way to read one. Until that happens these are proposals about how
  a chart could be read — implemented, and measured against the drawing — rather
  than answers.
- **Not a support commitment.** A bug in one of these is worth reporting, and
  reporting it is not a promise that the current behavior will be kept.

If you are building something that has to keep working, build it on the stable
set. If you are exploring what a chart could sound like, the experimental set is
exactly what it is for — and feedback on it is the thing that would move a type
out of this list.

## Bokeh support

Bokeh figures (`maidr.show(p)` on a `figure`, `gridplot`, `row` or `column`)
are read by an adapter that is itself **experimental**, whatever plot type it
emits: a Bokeh bar chart emits the stable `bar` type, but which glyphs are read
as what, the highlight drawn inside the Bokeh plot, and what is skipped may
change without a deprecation period, including in a patch release. The tables
above describe the *types*; this is about the *reader of Bokeh documents*, which
has not been through a user study either. See the
[Bokeh gallery](examples-bokeh.qmd) for what it reads today
([#813](https://github.com/xability/py-maidr/issues/813)). That includes how
the page gets BokehJS: from Bokeh's CDN, or inlined from the installed package
with `use_cdn=False` so a saved page works offline.

## plotnine support

plotnine charts (`maidr.show(p)` on a `ggplot`) are read by an adapter that is
itself **experimental**, whatever plot type it emits: a plotnine bar chart emits
the stable `bar` type, but which geoms, stats and positions are read as what,
how a facet panel is titled, and what is skipped may change without a
deprecation period, including in a patch release. It reads each layer's data as
plotnine computed it rather than the shapes it drew, and each facet panel
becomes a subplot; a geom, a position such as a jitter, or a coordinate system
it does not read is left out with a warning naming it. A `geom_line` of recall
against precision, which it read as a `line` before, emits the experimental
`pr_curve`, as does such a `geom_path`. See the [plotnine gallery](examples-plotnine.qmd) for what it reads today
([#814](https://github.com/xability/py-maidr/issues/814)). Install it with
`pip install "maidr[plotnine]"`.

## Excel support

Charts read out of an Excel workbook (`maidr.read_excel_charts("book.xlsx")`)
come through a reader that is itself **experimental**, whatever plot type it
emits: a column chart emits the stable `bar` type, but which Excel chart types
are read as what, how an axis with no title is named, how a date or a number
format is written, and what is skipped may change without a deprecation
period, including in a patch release. Each chart is read from the copy of its
values Excel keeps in the file and drawn again with matplotlib, and the reader
follows that drawing, which keeps the workbook's colors and titles but is not
Excel's own picture. Every chart type Excel draws is read; a histogram's bins
and a box's quartiles are worked out as Excel works them out, and a map is read
as the list of its regions, without their shapes. A chart part it cannot read
is left out with a warning naming it. See the
[Excel gallery](examples-excel.qmd) for what it reads today.

## PowerPoint and Word support

Charts read out of a PowerPoint presentation
(`maidr.read_powerpoint_charts("deck.pptx")`) or a Word document
(`maidr.read_word_charts("report.docx")`) come through the same
**experimental** reader as Excel's, whatever plot type it emits: a chart on a
slide or in a document is the chart part Excel draws, and it is read as the
[Excel support](#excel-support) section describes, from the copy of its values
the file keeps, with the workbook embedded beside it read only for the cells
that copy leaves out. How a presentation's slides and a document's charts are
ordered and named, and which parts of a document are read -- its body, not its
headers, footers, footnotes or comments -- may change without a deprecation
period too. See the [PowerPoint and Word gallery](examples-office.qmd) for what
it reads today.

## TensorBoard support

The charts read out of a TensorBoard log directory
(`maidr.read_tensorboard_scalars("logs")`,
`maidr.read_tensorboard_distributions("logs")`,
`maidr.read_tensorboard_histograms("logs")`,
`maidr.read_tensorboard_pr_curves("logs")` and
`maidr.read_tensorboard_graph("logs")`) come through a reader that is
itself **experimental**, whatever type it emits: a scalar chart emits the
stable `line` type, a distribution chart the experimental `percentile_band`,
a histogram the experimental `ridgeline`, PR curves the experimental
`pr_curve` and a Keras model's graph the experimental `directed_graph`, but how runs
and tags become charts, how smoothing is drawn, how a long run is thinned, how
a histogram is binned, and what is skipped may change without a deprecation
period, including in a patch release. Distributions and PR curves were read
as the stable `line` type, nine lines and a line per run, until maidr.js
gained the `percentile_band` and `pr_curve` traces; they changed type then. Each
tag's values are read from the event files, the values TensorBoard reads, and
drawn again with matplotlib; the reader follows that drawing, not
TensorBoard's own. Scalars and histograms are
read today, the Keras model graph (not TensorFlow's op-level graph), PR curves, a profile's step-time graph and top operations
(with `xprof` installed), and distributions from the histograms and hyperparameter sweeps
from the HParams plugin's summaries, and the Embedding Projector's
embeddings, and a **maidr** tab in TensorBoard shows them all
(`pip install "maidr[tensorboard]"`): images are tracked
in [#846](https://github.com/xability/py-maidr/issues/846). See the
[TensorBoard gallery](examples-tensorboard.qmd) for what it reads today.

## Keras support

The training curves drawn from a Keras model (`maidr.keras.plot_history()` and
`maidr.keras.MaidrCallback`) and the confusion matrix
(`maidr.keras.plot_confusion_matrix()`) are **experimental**, although every
chart they draw is a stable type, `line` or `heat`: how metrics become charts
and lines, what the lines are called, how predictions become classes, and when
the callback writes its page may change without a deprecation period,
including in a patch release. The PR curve (`maidr.keras.plot_pr_curve()`)
and the model graph (`maidr.keras.plot_model()`) are experimental twice over:
they emit the experimental `pr_curve` and `directed_graph` types -- the PR
curve was a stable `line` until maidr.js gained the `pr_curve` trace -- and
what a point or a layer is announced with, how a nested model becomes a
scope and how the graph is laid out may change the same way. See the
[Keras gallery](examples-keras.qmd) for what they draw today.

## Weights & Biases support {#weights-biases-support}

The training curves read from Weights & Biases runs
(`maidr.read_wandb_history()`) come through a reader that is **experimental**,
although every chart it draws is the stable `line` type: how runs and metrics
become charts and lines, what a line is called, how a run file is read, which
values count as numbers, and how a long run is thinned may change without a
deprecation period, including in a patch release. A run's file,
`run-<id>.wandb`, is read by maidr itself, by the format the W&B SDK writes
today, which is W&B's to change; a run fetched from the server is read through
`wandb.Api`. Numbers are read today: images, tables, histograms and W&B's
custom charts are not. See the [W&B gallery](examples-wandb.qmd) for what it
reads today.

## MLflow support

The training curves read from MLflow runs (`maidr.read_mlflow_metrics()`), and
the charts stored in a run (`maidr.log_mlflow_chart()`), are **experimental**,
although every chart drawn is the stable `line` type: how runs and metrics
become charts and lines, what a line is called, which metrics are left out,
and what the stored page holds may change without a deprecation period,
including in a patch release. See the [MLflow gallery](examples-mlflow.qmd)
for what it reads today.

## Drawn but not read

A few matplotlib calls draw marks that no `PlotType` reads, and that is
deliberate rather than a gap. Each registers nothing, so a figure holding only
that call falls back to a static picture, and a figure holding it beside a chart
that does read keeps that chart's reading untouched.

| call | why it is declined |
|---|---|
| `ax.quiver`, `ax.barbs`, `ax.streamplot` | a vector at a place carries a speed *and* a direction, and no trace holds both |
| `ax.triplot` | a mesh states which points were joined, not an order to walk |
| `ax.contourf`, `ax.tricontourf`, `ax.tripcolor` | a filled band spans two levels, so calling it one level's curve is right for half its vertices |
| `ax.fill` | a closed polygon states no series; it is asked for as a shape, not a sequence |
| `ax.axhline`, `ax.axvline`, `ax.axline`, `ax.axhspan`, `ax.axvspan` | a reference mark at a fixed position annotates a chart rather than being one |

`ax.table` draws no marks at all, so a figure holding only a table is reported
as empty, which is accurate.

Every other `Axes` method that draws marks is read as one of the types above:
`imshow`, `matshow`, `spy`, `specgram` and `hist2d` as `heat`; `stem`, `acorr` and `xcorr`
as `lollipop`; the spectra (`psd`, `csd`, `cohere`, `magnitude_spectrum`,
`angle_spectrum`, `phase_spectrum`) as `line`; `tricontour` as `contour`.
`tests/core/plot/test_unread_families.py` pins the whole sweep, so a call that
starts registering nothing, or a decline that starts registering something,
fails by name. The reasoning behind the `ax.fill` decline, the one that could be
overturned, is recorded there and in
[#685](https://github.com/xability/py-maidr/issues/685).

## How the split is derived

It is the diff of `PlotType` against `d9f7aee`, the last commit on `main` before
[#345](https://github.com/xability/py-maidr/issues/345) was filed:

```bash
git show d9f7aee:maidr/core/enum/plot_type.py | grep -oE '^\s+[A-Z_0-9]+ = "[a-z_0-9]+"'
```

`tests/core/test_plot_type_stability.py` fails if a member of `PlotType` appears
in neither table or in both, so a new plot type has to be placed deliberately
rather than inherit either promise by being forgotten.

## The same split upstream

The JavaScript core makes the same distinction over its own `TraceType`, with
the same boundary and for the same reason. See
[Trace type stability](https://maidr.ai/docs/SCHEMA.html#trace-type-stability) in the
core schema documentation.
